title: while loops

youtube.title: C++ while Loop: Repeat Until Done | C++ Programming EP 16
youtube.description: In this episode you will write a while loop, update the loop variable and predict the number of rounds, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 while loops · 0:52 A countdown · 1:32 Round by round · 2:02 Second program · 3:02 Recap · 3:33 Bug of the Day · 4:21 Challenge · 4:41 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "LOOP IT" in tomato on cream; Xecxec next to a crab running in a circle; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a crab running in a circle

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today your program learns to repeat. A loop does the same job again and again, with no copy and paste.

scenes.onScreen: "while loops": numbered lines (1. A loop repeats a block; 2. The test runs before each round; 3. Update the variable or the loop never ends) and an analogy card: a ceiling fan: it keeps turning while the switch is on
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A while loop repeats a block as long as its test is true. The test runs before every round. When the test is false, the loop ends. You must change the loop variable inside the body. If you do not, the test stays true, and the loop never ends. Think of a ceiling fan. It keeps turning while the switch is on.
points: The test runs before each round
Update the variable or the loop never ends

analogy.title: while loops
analogy.body: A ceiling fan: it keeps turning while the switch is on

scenes.onScreen: countdown.cpp: a while loop counts down from three
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 5] We start n at three. [HL 6] The loop tests whether n is greater than zero. [HL 7] It prints the value. [HL 8] Then n minus minus lowers n by one. [TRACK n=2] Now n is two, and the loop tests again. When n reaches zero, the test is false. [HL 10] The program prints Liftoff.

scenes.onScreen: a table of the rounds with the variable values
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: Here are the rounds. In round one, n is three and the test is true. In rounds two and three, the same happens. In round four, n is zero. The test is false, so the loop ends. Three rounds ran.

diagram.caption: a table of the rounds with the variable values

scenes.onScreen: total.cpp: a loop adds the numbers one to five
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 5] The counter i starts at one. [HL 6] The sum starts at zero. [HL 7] The loop runs while i is at most five. [HL 8] Each round adds i to the sum. [TRACK sum=3] After two rounds the sum is three. [HL 9] Then i goes up by one. [HL 11] At the end, the sum is fifteen.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as total dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints Sum colon fifteen.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A while loop repeats while its test is true. Two. The test runs before every round. Three. Change the loop variable inside the body. Four. Check the first and the last round, to avoid off-by-one errors. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A while loop repeats while its test is true.
The test runs before every round.
Change the loop variable inside the body.
Check the first and the last round, to avoid off-by-one errors.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: An off-by-one error
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the program runs and the wrong output appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the output turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We want the sum of one to five. The program prints ten. The test says less than five, so the loop stops before it adds five. This is an off-by-one error. Check the first round and the last round by hand. Use less than or equal.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the loop go to the doctor? It had a problem with its condition, and it kept coming back.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: Why did the loop go to the doctor? It had a problem with its condition, and it kept coming back.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: print a table of two
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Use a while loop to print the table of two, from two times one to two times ten. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: for loops. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Program output (it runs, but the answer is wrong):

Sum: 10
bug.why: With less than five, the loop stops before it adds five. The sum is ten, not fifteen.

pun: "Why did the loop go to the doctor? It had a problem with its condition, and it kept coming back."
challenge: Use a while loop to print the table of two, from two times one to two times ten.
challengeAnswer: Start i at one. While i is at most ten, print two times i, and then add one to i.
